topic: Classless Interdomain Routing (CIDR) and Non-default Subnet Masks
reasoning: Roosevelt has already learned basic IPv4 addressing and network/host portions, so we must advance directly into CIDR notation and subnet mask calculations for his upcoming exam.

elements.text: Target Exam Date: Nov 9, 2026 (17 days left!)

segments.speech: Welcome to today's live class, Roosevelt. Your exam is in seventeen days, so we are stepping up our networking game. Today we master CIDR notation and non-default subnet masks.

elements.text: Expressing subnet masks via prefix length (e.g., /24)

segments.speech: Notice how CIDR completely replaces rigid classful addressing. Instead of writing out 255.255.255.0 every single time, we append slash twenty-four to show the network prefix length.

elements.text: Remember to subtract 2 for the network and broadcast addresses!

segments.speech: Let's apply this to a practical example. If we have a /24 network, we use the formula two to the power of thirty-two minus n, minus two, to find our usable host count.

elements.text: Core Rule: Host bits = 32 - prefix length. Total Hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2.
Review these formulas before your November exam, Roosevelt!

segments.speech: To wrap up, Roosevelt, always remember that your host bits determine your subnet size using two to the power of un minus two. Review this core concept before your exam in November!
